title: Sai Silks (Kalamandir) Ltd - 543989 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Analyst / Investor Meet - Outcome

summary.headline: Sai Silks FY26 revenue rose 13.1% to INR1,654 crore and PAT to INR141 crore; management guides FY27 revenue above FY26 on ~1 lakh sq ft net retail addition.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue was about INR419 crore, up 5.1% YoY, with PAT of INR32.65 crore versus INR13.51 crore a year earlier. Q4 EBITDA margin was about 14.6% as advertising and employee costs (bonus, Labour Code, stores opened late in the quarter) weighed, despite gross margin at 42.08%. For FY26, EBITDA margin rose to 15.76% from 14.48%, same-store sales growth was about 3%, and the company ended with 81 stores (from 68) and about 785,000 sq ft. Management guided FY27 net addition of about 1 lakh sq ft, SSSG similar to or slightly better than FY26, and EBITDA margin of at least 17.5% to 18%.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR85 crore YoY (~+65%); prior year operational PAT about INR105 crore excluding one-time tax

segments.name: Varamahalakshmi (VML)
segments.commentary: About 52% of FY26 sales per management, and its share is rising; it is the best-margin format, and Tamil Nadu productivity is expected to improve 5-10% YoY. High single-digit SSSG in Telangana and Andhra Pradesh.

segments.name: Kalamandir
segments.commentary: Leads FY27 expansion in Karnataka (Bangalore focus); planned FY27 format mix is roughly 60:40 Kalamandir to VML. Management says it has lower margins but higher turnover.

segments.name: KLM
segments.commentary: Declined about 3% in FY26; more than 60-65% of KLM stores are in Telangana, which drives the state's slowdown. One 9,000 sq ft KLM store capacity was cut; no KLM stores are planned for FY27.

segments.name: State-wise
segments.commentary: Telangana sales fell from about INR600 crore (FY23) to INR500 crore (FY26). Andhra Pradesh rose to INR474 crore from INR443 crore; AP grew about 15% and Karnataka about 27% per management.

guidance_outlook: FY27 net retail addition of about 1 lakh sq ft (at least 20% above FY26's ~78,600 sq ft gross addition); management may update at H1 and says it could go beyond 1 lakh.
FY27 SSSG expected similar to or slightly better than FY26's ~3%.
FY27 revenue growth to be better than FY26's 13.1%; no numeric revenue guidance, to be updated after H1.
FY27 EBITDA margin at least 17.5% to 18% (company said it was about 16 points in FY26); full-year EBITDA margin up at least 50 bps is also cited.
No new borrowings expected this year or for the next 2-3 years; company is debt-free and expects to fund expansion internally.
H2 FY27 expected to be stronger than H1; April 2026 growth was low single-digit positive. Adhik Maas to slow Q1 until mid-June; Dussehra moved into Q3. Advertising to stay around 4% of sales.
Plans to enter at least one new state this year (Maharashtra/Mumbai discussed); about 5-10% more wedding dates in FY27 than FY26.
capex_capacity: FY26: 13 new stores and 1 extension added (68 to 81 stores across 5 South Indian states); ~78,600 sq ft added, net ~69,000 sq ft, total ~785,000 sq ft.
Q4 FY26: about 24,000 sq ft added, with a 9,000 sq ft capacity reduction at one KLM store (no closures). Two Q4 stores (about 25,000 sq ft) opened March 10-15, so they added little Q4 revenue.
Payback for a Varamahalakshmi store is 8-9 months; maturity to company-average EBITDA margin takes about 1.5-2 years (longer for Kalamandir).
Depreciation fell in Q4 due to Ind AS 116 lease workings; it will rise as FY27 leases are signed.
Inventory rose only INR34 crore despite about 70,000 sq ft added; inventory per sq ft fell from about INR11,533 (FY24) to about INR10,480.
demand_pricing: Wedding calendar is comfortable and spread across quarters; absolute wedding dates are 5-10% higher than last year.
Management said late January to February 2026 consumption slowed, linked to geopolitical and consumption factors, and this drove Q4's flat-ish growth.
Gold price increases and duty hikes are reportedly shifting some wedding budgets to sarees; saree budgets are reported to have fallen from about INR1 lakh to INR60,000-70,000.
Tamil Nadu store averages were about INR32,300 per sq ft for FY26 and were about INR95-98 crore per quarter in recent quarters; management expects a 5-10% YoY improvement.
Management flagged rising competitive intensity, faster fashion cycles and digital influence. It plans hyperlocal marketing and assortment corrections for weaker catchments.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the company not appeal the INR21 crore company tax demand when the promoter's ~INR50 crore demand was dropped?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said the company's matter was settled last year (Q4 FY25) after it agreed to the demand on COVID-era employee advances. The promoter demand was a separate personal matter that was dropped after appeal; management said it was not a waiver.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Q4 growth slowdown linked to Valli store additions?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no. H1/H2 revenue split was 51:49 in FY26. Q4 slowed on late-January to February consumption, and two stores opened in mid-March contributed little revenue.

qa_highlights.question: What was the EBITDA margin squeeze in Q4 and will it recur?
qa_highlights.answer: Advertising fell about INR10 crore YoY but some spend landed in Q4. Employee costs rose from store openings (50-55% of new space opened Dec 15-Mar 15), bonus (about INR4 crore in Q4, about 2 bps) and Labour Code effects. Bonus costs fall in H1.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 expansion split across states and formats?
qa_highlights.answer: Most pipeline stores are in Karnataka, led by Kalamandir. VML is coming in Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu. Format mix is about 60:40 Kalamandir to VML, and at least one store will open outside core markets this year.

qa_highlights.question: What is the KLM and Telangana outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: KLM declined about 3% in FY26 and is being fixed by product mix changes; SSSG in Telangana was pulled down by KLM. VML SSSG in Telangana and AP is high single-digit.

qa_highlights.question: What EBITDA and PAT trajectory is implied for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated an EBITDA margin of at least 17.5-18% for FY27 and said debt-free status and no interest cost would lift PAT margin. It declined to give a PAT figure and said the mathematics would come at the Q2 call.

risks_watch: Q4 margin pressure: advertising and employee costs (bonus, Labour Code) are rising. Management is targeting a 17.5-18% EBITDA margin.
Telangana (about 60-65% KLM-weighted) and Tamil Nadu flattening; a KLM revival plan is still unproven.
Inventory days remain high (about 180 days last year); no formal target was set.
Gold price and duty effects on wedding spend; saree ticket sizes are reported to be falling.
Store openings clustered late in quarters hurt in-quarter revenue; FY27 guidance depends on H1 update on store count.
Depreciation will rise with new lease contracts; new-state entry may need higher advertising.
summary.management_tone: Confident on long-term structural demand and margin ambition, but cautious and non-committal on numeric FY27 revenue and PAT, deferring figures to the H1 and Q2 updates. Defensive on the Q4 margin dip and the tax matters, which it attributed to timing and to closed matters.
key_quotes: We still delivered strong double -digit revenue growth, significant profitabilit y improvement, sustained margin expansion and also focused on our retail expansion.
One of the top high priority KPIs for us is to maintain the gross margin irrespective of the fact we are coming with the newer formats and lesser gross margin stores.
It's not about the resources , but consider that we have never closed the stores on account of operational issues.
The challenge is to be able to identify carefully, handpick carefully and be able to handhold these stores.

adds.what: ~1 lakh sq ft net retail addition in FY27 (Kalamandir-led, Karnataka/Bangalore focus; at least 20% above FY26's ~78,600 sq ft gross addition)

growth.why: Management guides FY27 revenue growth above FY26's 13.1% (no numeric figure), backed by ~1 lakh sq ft net retail addition (about 12.7% of ~785,000 sq ft base), SSSG of ~3%+, and wedding dates up 5-10%; no specific FY27 store timeline or order-level detail given, so backing is partial.
